title: A Wallet on the Ground
description:
Under a bench at a bus stop. A wallet.
Pick it up. Inside — ₩300,000 in cash, an ID, a few cards.
Nobody nearby. No CCTV in sight.

{name}'s account barely covers this month's rent.
₩300,000 would breathe for a few days.
Conscience and hunger are sitting on the same palm.

choices.text: Take it to the police.  (clear conscience + reputation / time + no cash)
choices.result_text: I walked out of the police station with a receipt. The way back felt strangely light.

choices.text: Keep the cash. Drop the wallet in a mailbox.  (₩300,000 / guilt)
choices.result_text:
{name} pocketed the cash and pushed the wallet into the nearest mailbox.
The ID would get back to its owner — that was the justification.
₩300,000 appeared. That night, the food didn't go down well.
Crossing a small line once makes the next line easier.

choices.text: Walk past. Don't touch it either way.  (do nothing / unease)
choices.result_text:
{name} moved on without looking back.
Neither took the money nor took responsibility.
On the bus, couldn't stop thinking about that wallet.
Doing nothing is also a choice.

title: After Returning It
description:
Left the wallet at the station and walked away. A few days later, a call.
The owner — a middle-aged business owner, grateful, asking to meet.
"In this day and age, there are still people like you. Let me at least buy you a meal."

choices.text: Accept the gesture graciously.  (connection + token / awkward meeting)
choices.result_text:
Awkward — but {name} showed up.
The owner pressed a thank-you into {name}'s hand and offered a business card.
"Character is an asset. If you ever need anything, call."
An honest pair of hands brought an unexpected connection.

choices.text: "It was the right thing to do" — politely decline.  (self-respect / connection + cash)
choices.result_text:
{name} waved off the reward. It was just the right thing.
The owner was more moved than before — but the connection stayed light.
Kept the conscience. Nothing to hold in the hand. Still felt light.

title: The Offer
description:
A message from an old coworker.
"Come to our startup. 1.5x your current salary.
We just closed Series A — if it works out, the stock options could change everything.
Of course — fifty-fifty chance of folding in two years, but."

Current job is dull but stable.
{name}'s ₩3 billion is impossibly far on this dull monthly paycheck.

choices.text: Take the leap. Leave stability behind.  (higher pay + opportunity / risk + stability)
choices.result_text: I held out my resignation letter. The team lead was silent for a moment, then just said, "Understood."

choices.text: Decline. Hold this position.  (stability / opportunity + regret)
choices.result_text:
{name} chose the safe option. The reassurance of a reliable paycheck each month.
But months later, when that startup hit the news with a new funding round —
'Should I have gone?' followed {name} around for days.
The cost of the safe road is the lingering what-if.

choices.text: Ask for more time to decide.  (careful / risk of losing the slot)
choices.result_text:
{name} said "let me think for a few days."
Pulled the financials, asked around about their reputation. Thorough.
In the meantime — the spot went to someone else.
Look before you leap — but too much looking and you never cross.

title: The Bet
description:
{name} handed in the resignation. Gave up a steady paycheck by choice.
The new office was energetic; everyone's eyes were alive.
And — twice the late nights. The future in a fog.
That sheet of stock options: will it become kindling or a new life?

choices.text: Go all in. Day and night, no holding back.  (growth + equity / health + burnout)
choices.result_text:
{name} ground through it. The company grew fast, and so did the equity value.
But health bottomed out, and the face in the mirror was always exhausted.
The price of limitless opportunity is always paid in body and time.

choices.text: Keep a sustainable pace.  (sustainable / drift from core)
choices.result_text:
{name} decided not to overextend. Kept health intact, kept showing up steadily.
Avoided burnout — but drifted slightly from the core team over time.
To last, you have to protect something — and that means giving something up too.
